When the storm held off for an hour longer than sense allowed, Marcus disliked the mercy of it. Delay at sea is a language, and it often says that a worse thing is gathering its breath. The men on the pier joked without mirth and tightened knots that had no need of tightening. Marcus checked the boats, then checked the men, and found the boats more reliable company. A child ran along the quay with a length of blue cord trailing behind him like a banner surrendered by mistake. His mother called him back sharply, and the sound carried farther than it should have in such weather. Marcus marked that in his mind. One never knows which small domestic note will remain after the louder alarms have spent themselves.
